accepted.s: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) was launched in which year with an outlay of approximately ₹20,050 crore?
accepted.x: PMMSY was launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹20,050 crore.
accepted.tq: Use the year–outlay pair to eliminate nearby-year distractors.
accepted.sec: Fisheries - PMMSY and PM-MKSSY, MPEDA, fisheries growth rate, AP rank in aquaculture and shrimp  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the duration of PMMSY:
1. It was initially implemented from FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25.
2. Its implementation was extended up to FY 2025-26.
3. It is administered by the Department of Fisheries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: PMMSY initially covered FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25, was extended to FY 2025-26, and is administered by the Department of Fisheries.
accepted.tq: Check the scheme period, extension and administering department separately.
accepted.sec: Fisheries - PMMSY and PM-MKSSY, MPEDA, fisheries growth rate, AP rank in aquaculture and shrimp  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institution is responsible for training and capacity building under PMMSY?
o: Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund
accepted.x: The National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) handles training and capacity building under PMMSY.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific implementing institution rather than the parent department.
accepted.sec: Fisheries - PMMSY and PM-MKSSY, MPEDA, fisheries growth rate, AP rank in aquaculture and shrimp  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to PMMSY funding, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Centrally Sponsored component in North-Eastern and Himalayan States — 90:10 Centre-State funding
Centrally Sponsored component in general States — 90:10 Centre-State funding
Central Sector component — 60:40 Centre-State funding for all States
Centrally Sponsored component in Union Territories — 60:40 Centre-State funding
accepted.x: The Centrally Sponsored component follows a 90:10 Centre-State ratio in North-Eastern and Himalayan States. The general ratio is 60:40, while Union Territories receive 100% central funding.
accepted.tq: Split the options by funding category and beneficiary region.
accepted.sec: Fisheries - PMMSY and PM-MKSSY, MPEDA, fisheries growth rate, AP rank in aquaculture and shrimp  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is covered under the Central Sector component of PMMSY?
o: Production subsidy exclusively for general States
accepted.x: The Central Sector component includes training, quarantine, harbour modernisation and data systems.
accepted.tq: Match the activity with the correct scheme component.
accepted.sec: Fisheries - PMMSY and PM-MKSSY, MPEDA, fisheries growth rate, AP rank in aquaculture and shrimp  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM-MKSSY is best described as:
o: A Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY for formalising fisheries and supporting fisheries micro-enterprises
A fund exclusively for constructing fishing harbours
A Centrally Sponsored scheme for horticultural exports
A programme for inland river ranching under Namami Gange
accepted.x: PM-MKSSY, or Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana, is a Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY aimed at formalising the fisheries sector and supporting fisheries micro-enterprises.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a sub-scheme’s purpose from related fisheries programmes.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s position in aquaculture and farmed-shrimp production?
o: It is the second-largest producer, with only tiger shrimp being produced.
It is the largest producer of marine fish but not farmed shrimp.
It is the fourth-largest producer, with trout as the main variety.
It is the largest producer, with Vannamei as the predominant farmed shrimp variety.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is the largest aquaculture and farmed-shrimp producer, with Vannamei being the predominant variety.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh fisheries:

accepted.s: Which statement regarding cold-water fisheries is correct?

They are confined exclusively to Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
